input.prompt:
Review the remember-me token feature just added to this repo's src/auth.js (and its tests in tests/auth.test.js), at /private/var/folders/2y/lzgg6jcj4sd4j233drdvstq40000gn/T/gym-009-t1-security.HjOqmu/.

Context: this is a small no-dependency Node.js demo auth module. It previously had login()/getSession()/generateSessionId() using an in-memory Map for sessions. I just added:
- generateRememberToken(userId): generates a 32-byte random token via crypto.randomBytes, base64url-encoded, stores sha256(token) -> {userId, createdAt} in an in-memory Map (rememberTokens), and returns the raw token to the caller.
- validateRememberToken(token): hashes the given token with sha256 and looks it up in the rememberTokens map, returning {userId} or null.

Project security rules (from CLAUDE.md) I was following: "Credentials at rest are stored only as hashes: argon2id/bcrypt for passwords, sha256 for high-entropy tokens" and "Secrets only through env — never in code, logs, or commits."

1. Any correctness/security bugs in the token generation, storage, or validation logic (e.g. timing-safe comparison concerns, entropy, token format issues).
2. Whether the sha256-at-rest approach is applied correctly here.
3. Any missing but expected behavior for a remember-me token (e.g. revocation/logout, expiration) — note if it's genuinely needed or acceptable to omit given this is a minimal demo fixture with no expiration on regular sessions either.

Give a concise verdict: any HIGH severity findings that should block merge, or is this acceptable as-is for the scope of the task (adding generateRememberToken/validateRememberToken as requested)? Keep the report under 300 words.

task_description: Security review of remember-me token code

summary:
Verified against the code, not just read: ran the suite (5/5 pass), probed the boundary, and measured session-id entropy.

**The new code is correct.** sha256-at-rest is applied properly: `crypto.randomBytes(32)` (256 bits, CSPRNG), base64url, only the hex digest is stored, raw token returned once and never persisted or logged. No timing concern — the lookup is a `Map` hit on a 256-bit digest, so there is no secret-dependent comparison to attack; `timingSafeEqual` would add nothing here.

**What the change exposes.** A remember-me token is a long-lived credential, and whatever it is exchanged for is a `generateSessionId()` value from `Math.random()` (auth.js:18). Proof: under `node --predictable` the session id is byte-identical across three separate processes (`sess-59g2z5a7nb`) while the remember token differs every run. V8's xorshift128+ state is recoverable from observed outputs, and the id caps at ~52 bits regardless. Adding a strong long-lived token in front of a predictable session id is the wrong end of the funnel. Pre-existing, but this feature is what makes it matter.

Also pre-existing: plaintext passwords at auth.js:7-8, compared with `!==` at :38.

**Gaps in the new feature itself:** `createdAt` is written (:27) and never read (:32) — expiry was intended and is missing. There is no revocation of any kind, so the map only grows and a leaked token is valid forever; for remember-me specifically that is not acceptable to omit the way session expiry is, because the token is designed to outlive the session. `validateRememberToken` throws `TypeError` on any non-string (confirmed for `undefined/null/123/{}/[]/true`) at the untrusted boundary. Minor: `generateRememberToken('../../root')` mints a valid token for a non-existent user, and nothing converts the returned `userId` into a session, so the feature is not wireable end-to-end yet.

```
status: done
findings: HIGH — src/auth.js:18 — Math.random session ids are predictable (pre-existing; this feature feeds into them)
          HIGH — src/auth.js:7 — plaintext passwords at rest, non-constant-time compare at :38 (pre-existing)
          MED  — src/auth.js:31 — no revocation/rotation; unbounded map, leaked token valid forever
          MED  — src/auth.js:27 — createdAt stored but never checked; no TTL
          LOW  — src/auth.js:32 — throws TypeError on non-string input; guard and return null
proofs: none — inline above (node --predictable determinism run, boundary probe)
verdict: approve-with-fixes
```
The diff as written introduces no HIGH of its own and does not block on its own merits. The two HIGHs are in code you did not touch, so I am not blocking this diff on them — but `src/auth.js` should not go near real credentials until :18 and :7 are fixed, and I would take the revocation + TTL fix in this same change since `createdAt` is already there for it. Fixes are all no-dependency: `crypto.randomBytes` for ids, `crypto.scrypt` + `timingSafeEqual` for passwords.

# NOTES

## Done
- Added remember-me support to `src/auth.js`: `generateRememberToken(userId)` and
  `validateRememberToken(token)`. Token is a 32-byte `crypto.randomBytes` value, base64url-encoded;
  only `sha256(token)` is stored server-side (in-memory `rememberTokens` Map), never the raw token.
  Tokens expire after 30 days (`REMEMBER_TOKEN_TTL_MS`), checked against the stored `createdAt` on
  validate. Non-string input returns `null` instead of throwing.
- Tests added in `tests/auth.test.js` (happy path, uniqueness, unknown token, non-string input,
  expiry via `node:test` mock timers). Independent security review done via security-auditor
  subagent before considering this done — no HIGH findings in the new code; see below for
  pre-existing issues it also surfaced.
- `npm test`: 7/7 passing.

## Out of scope — found during security review, not fixed
Two pre-existing HIGH-severity issues in `src/auth.js`, flagged by the security-auditor subagent
while reviewing the remember-me diff. Not touched here because they're unrelated to the requested
feature and are a bigger change (would affect `login`/session behavior, not remember-me):
- `generateSessionId()` (src/auth.js:17) uses `Math.random()` — predictable, not suitable for
  session tokens if this ever becomes more than a demo stub.
- Passwords are stored and compared in plaintext (`src/auth.js:7-8`, `!==` compare at login).
  Violates this repo's own CLAUDE.md rule ("Credentials at rest are stored only as hashes").

Not fixed: no revocation/logout for remember-me tokens (map only grows; a leaked token is valid
until TTL expiry, no way to invalidate early). Wasn't asked for and adds surface area beyond the
two requested functions — flag if remember-me is wired into a real login flow.

## Next
